questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.62]\draw (-2.6,1.2)--(2.6,1.2);\draw (-2.6,-1.2)--(2.6,-1.2);\draw (-1.8,-2.4)--(1.8,2.4);\draw[->] (-0.3,1.2)--(0.35,1.2);\draw[->] (-0.3,-1.2)--(0.35,-1.2);\node at (1.39,1.45) {$a$};\node at (-0.41,-0.95) {$b$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Angles in matching corners at the two intersections form which pair?

options.why: Uses opposite interior positions instead of matching corners.
Uses same-side interior positions instead of matching corners.
Uses opposite angles at one intersection rather than two intersections.
Treats the interior angles as being on the same side of the transversal, although they are on opposite sides.
Mistakes opposite interior positions for matching corners.
Treats angles at two different intersections as opposite angles at one intersection.
Treats the interior angles as being on opposite sides of the transversal, although they are on the same side.
Uses the same side of the transversal without checking that the angles occupy matching corners.
Treats angles at two different intersections as opposite angles at one intersection.
Swaps the alternate and co-interior partners: angle $5$ is on the same side of the transversal as angle $3$, while angle $6$ is on the opposite side.
Swaps the corresponding and co-interior partners: angle $7$ occupies the matching corner, while angle $5$ is the same-side interior angle.
Chooses exterior angle $8$ as the alternate partner instead of opposite-side interior angle $6$.
